name: Dolly Dimpler

lead:
The Dolly Dimpler was a mechanical dimple-making device advertised in Photoplay magazine in April 1926. It belongs to a history of products for creating cheek dimples, which have long been associated with youth, charm and a cheerful smile.
No clinical studies exist on the Dolly Dimpler. Wikipedia notes that for the later Dimple Maker (1936) it is unknown whether any effect lasted.

paras: Period devices of this type were spring or brace designs that pressed small knobs into the cheeks. The details of the Dolly Dimpler's use are not documented.

No safety data exist. Wikipedia reports that the American Medical Association argued frequent users of the later Dimple Maker could develop cancer. Cosmetic surgery for dimples (dimpleplasty) is the modern clinical route.

lead: The Dolly Dimpler was a device marketed in the 1920s to create dimples. Wikipedia states that it was advertised in the April 1926 issue of Photoplay [1].

Dimples are commonly linked to youth, beauty and a more cheerful smile, which explains the appeal of products that promised them [1]. A later device, the 1936 Dimple Maker invented by Isabella Gilbert, was a face-fitted metal brace that pressed dents into the cheeks [1].
No published research has examined the Dolly Dimpler.

paras: Cheek dimples usually sit on mobile tissue and may come from a double or split zygomaticus major muscle. They are widely linked with youth and attractiveness, and Chinese culture treats them as a good-luck sign [1].

The Dolly Dimpler was advertised in Photoplay in April 1926. A later device, Isabella Gilbert's 1936 Dimple Maker, was a metal brace fitted to the face. Wikipedia says it is unknown whether its effect lasted and that the AMA argued frequent users could develop cancer [1].
Cosmetic dimple surgery became available from the 1960s after Khoo Boo-Chai published a technique in 1962, and a 2017 Independent article reported rising numbers of millennials seeking it [1].
